semiconductors.summary: Semis rallied sharply on Thursday, with SOXX +8.15%, as hyperscaler capex raises and memory-cost inflation repriced demand. NVDA, MU, and AMD recovered but all remain below their 50-day averages — the cluster is a bounce, not a trend. China self-sufficiency fears (CXMT listing, domestic DUV) are the structural overhang capping upside until resolved.

semiconductors.key_development: Amazon's capex raise citing higher memory costs confirms the memory-price passthrough and supports demand for HBM/NAND, but Chinese lithography progress introduces a multi-quarter margin risk.

big_tech.summary: BigTech diverged: MSFT surged 6% after Azure beat and capex spend narrative, while META dropped further as its own capex raise without cloud monetization spooked investors. AMZN beat and guided higher capex, benefiting the supply chain. The sector's AI monetization gap remains the key fault line.

active_risks.text: US-Iran Hormuz blockade persists but de-escalating — some vessels pass, ceasefire framework proposed.
US-China AI chip war escalates as China develops domestic immersion DUV lithography and CXMT raises $8.6B in record IPO.
Fed hawkish hold with three dissents signals a split, raising September rate hike odds; oil price volatility feeds into inflation expectations.

geopolitical.market_impact: Hormuz de-escalation is pulling oil lower (WTI $82.34), easing inflation fears and supporting a tech rally. However, China's domestic DUV and CXMT listing are repricing the memory and semi supply chain, capping upside for names like MU and ASML. Hyperscaler capex raises (AMZN, MSFT) offset some of this, but the structural overhang from Chinese competition persists.

optimistic.description: US-Iran ceasefire is signed, WTI drops to $75-80, removing the main inflation driver. Fed tone eases, rate hike odds collapse. pessimistic.description: Hormuz escalates again, WTI spikes to $100+. Fed forced to hike in September, crushing tech multiples. Chinese DUV tool gains more traction, ASML and MU underperform. META capex fears deepen, dragging BigTech. Semis fall back to recent lows; SG banks sell off on rate shock.

wildcard.description: A breakthrough in US-China AI talks leads to a partial easing of export controls, boosting semis and ASML. However, this also cements China's domestic chip capabilities, creating long-term competitive threats. Oil stays rangebound, VIX drops to 15.
